reportOnly: REPORT ONLY. No apply is authorized, no lane is armed, and no relocation list is offered. Drew asked for a census and a recommendation; this is the census and the recommendation. Implementing the move is a separate decision.
finding: 1,129 sold_comps rows are addressed by a `backstop:` key, which is NOT the slug grammar. `backstop:<player>|<year>||<parallel>` names no card the pricing path can read: computeHobbyIqCardId emits `hiq:sport:year:setKey:cardNumber:parallel:auto[:num-N]`, every pool read keys on that shape, and a row outside it prices nothing. This is an ADDRESS defect, not a grade or identity defect -- the rows' own fields are mostly sound.
whyItSurfacedNow: The I9 triage cited `backstop:michael jordan|1986||` as evidence for the proposed graded-from-title re-key: a pool holding PSA 9 OC, PSA 5 and PSA 8 sales 'under one raw address'. The read-only census showed the opposite of the premise -- the grade FIELDS on those rows are already correct and complete (PSA 8/9/7/6/5/4/3, one PSA 0, one PSA 8.5), so `filterByGrade` would separate them correctly the moment the rows had a readable address. Nothing about that pool is a grade defect. What it is, is 183 sales of the most valuable basketball rookie card there is, parked at an address no reader can price.

census.method: read-only, one cross-partition query bounded by STARTSWITH(c.cardId,'backstop:') (1,129 rows, 84 RU), plus card_catalog point reads on the most-populated candidate destinations.

shape.note: `derivableShaped` counts rows carrying a setName, a cardNumber and a cardYear -- the three inputs a slug needs beyond sport. It is an UPPER BOUND on what a rematch could address, not a verdict: the real deriver normalizes the setKey and applies slugGuard, and neither was run here. The 302 rows with no cardNumber cannot be addressed at all without a checklist lookup by player.

observations: EVERY ROW IS `source: cardsight`, and Cardsight is RETIRED from matching (off in code 2026-08-16; prod env vars inert but set). No new rows arrive at these keys. The population is closed and will not grow.

THE KEYS COLLAPSE DISTINCT CARDS. `backstop:eric hartman|2026||blue refractor` holds sales whose own setName field says `bowman`, `bowman-chrome` AND `topps`, and whose titles name Gold Refractor, Aqua Refractor /125 and plain 1st Bowman Chrome Auto. One backstop key is several cards -- so this is not merely a wrong address, it is a SPLIT POOL under a shared one, and a relocation must separate them rather than move them together.
THE GRADE FIELDS ARE NOT THE DEFECT. 632 of 1,129 rows carry grade fields, and on the Jordan key they are complete and correct across nine grades. A grade lane has nothing to do here.

THE VALUE IS CONCENTRATED. The top 10 keys hold 651 of 1,129 rows (58%), and two of them -- a 1986 Fleer Sticker Jordan rookie and a 2020 Justin Herbert -- are cards with deep, liquid comp pools ALREADY EXISTING at their proper addresses. These sales are not pricing a card that has no other data; they are missing from pools that would readily absorb them.

recommendation.verdict: RE-ADDRESS the derivable rows through the GREAT REMATCH; RETIRE nothing yet; do NOT build a bespoke lane.
recommendation.why: A whole-source retire is the wrong instrument twice over. First, `feedback_replaced_by_is_product_level_coverage_is_per_card`: coverage is measured per card, and these 1,129 rows are real observed sales -- retiring them deletes market evidence for a 1986 Fleer Sticker Jordan rookie to tidy an address. Second, `feedback_a_whole_source_retire_needs_its_name`: cardsight being retired from MATCHING says nothing about whether its already-ingested SALES are true. The sales happened.
proposedPath: 1. NOT A NEW SCOPE. The existing rematch already re-derives an identity from the title and re-keys the row; a `backstop:` row is simply one whose stored address is unreadable rather than wrong-but-parseable. What it needs is for the census to REACH it -- the shard axis is (cardYear, sportClass, sha1(id) % parts) and these rows carry cardYear, so they are already shardable.

2. THE BLOCKER IS THE CLASS, NOT THE LANE. `slugYearSegment` returns null for a non-`hiq:` key and the eviction/improve gates read the stored slug, so these rows classify UNDERIVABLE or CONFLICT today. Deciding what class a non-grammar address belongs to is a ruling, and it is the one thing this report does not presume.

3. SEPARATE BEFORE MOVING. Because one backstop key holds several cards (see observations), any move must be per-ROW off the title, never per-KEY. A key-level relocation list would merge three Eric Hartman parallels into one pool and create exactly the defect `feedback_one_card_one_row_one_pool` forbids.

4. THE 302 ROWS WITH NO cardNumber ARE A SEPARATE QUESTION. They cannot be addressed from their own fields and would need a checklist lookup by player and year. Report them; do not guess a number for them -- CF-UNPARSED-IS-NOT-UNNUMBERED.

5. MEASURE THE DESTINATIONS FIRST. This report deliberately did not run the real deriver (that needs the parser and slugGuard, i.e. a census pass, not a point query). Before any ruling, a report-first census slot should print: how many of the 739 derive a slug that passes slugGuard, how many of those destinations are checklist-backed, and how many already hold sales -- the same three numbers #1890 produced for the vintage-year class.

notRecommended.retireTheRows: Deletes real sales, including 183 on a Jordan rookie, to fix an address. Refused unless Drew rules the cardsight sales themselves untrustworthy -- which is a claim about the SALES, and nothing measured here supports it.
notRecommended.keyLevelRelocationList: One backstop key is several cards. A list keyed on the backstop address would merge them.
notRecommended.leaveAsIs: These rows are invisible to every pool read, so they contribute nothing to any FMV while still counting as corpus rows -- the worst of both.
